text:
The Rangers visit the Devils tonight with the model calling it close, projecting 3.08 expected goals for NYR and 2.98 for NJD. The two teams have been built differently so far. New Jersey creates the better chances, generating 3.74 expected goals per 60 against 3.39 for New York, and it owns 60 percent of the expected goals at five-on-five to the Rangers' 52. But NYR has turned its chances into results, scoring 3.38 goals a game and allowing just 1.75, while the Devils are scoring 2.67 and allowing 3.67 over six games. Both defenses allow a similar quality of chance (2.78 expected goals against per 60 for NYR, 2.89 for NJD), so the gap in goals against is mostly about what is happening in net.

That makes the goalie matchup the hinge of the night. Dylan Garand is the projected starter for NYR, with a .950 save percentage and 3.29 goals saved above expected in four games. He added 3.88 in three games last season. Jake Allen is the projected starter for NJD, sitting at .890 and minus 1.32 this year, though he was 5.39 above expected across 37 games last season. Special teams are close. The Rangers' power play averages 0.74 expected goals a game to 0.65 for the Devils, and New Jersey's penalty kill gives up 0.63 to NYR's 0.41, though New York takes 4.25 penalties a game to New Jersey's 2.83.

Both teams played last night with one day of rest. NYR has won four of its last five, with the lone loss at WSH. NJD has been up and down: a 6-0 loss at NYI, then a 4-1 win over VAN and an overtime win at DET in which it held 67 percent of the expected goals. The model likes Jack Hughes, who has a 34 percent chance to score and 29 percent for two or more points. For New York, it picks Alexis Lafrenière (34 percent to score) and Mika Zibanejad (30 percent to score, 27 percent for two-plus points).
